questions.question: What does a Poisson process model?
options: Sampling without replacement from a finite population
A single continuous value on a fixed interval
Random arrivals over time at a constant average rate
The median of a sample only

questions.question: What condition is required for the Poisson process rate $\lambda$?
What does $N_t$ usually count in a Poisson process?
options: The waiting time until the first arrival
The number of arrivals up to time $t$

questions.question: What distribution does $N_{t+s}-N_s$ have in a Poisson process?
What key independence property does a Poisson process have?
Which situation may be approximated by a Poisson process during a stable period?
options: The number of aces in a card hand
The sorted median of a sample

questions.question: Particle emissions from a radioactive source are often modeled as what?
If a Poisson process has rate $\lambda=3$, what is the distribution of arrivals in an interval of length $2$?
Requests to a server over short intervals may be modeled as what?
In a Poisson process, what kind of distribution do interarrival times have?
What does it mean that the number of arrivals depends only on interval length?
options: Counts depend on the starting time even under stable rate
Only intervals starting at zero are allowed
Counts are deterministic once the length is known
Intervals of the same length have the same count distribution

questions.question: Why is a Poisson process a stochastic process?
options: It is only a fixed sample median.
It is a family of counts indexed by time

questions.question: How are Poisson distribution and Poisson process related?
options: The process has no count distributions
Counts over time intervals have Poisson distributions
Poisson distributions only describe waiting times.
The process is a finite population sample

questions.question: If $\lambda=5$ per hour, what is the distribution of arrivals in half an hour?
If two disjoint time intervals are considered in a Poisson process, what is true about their arrival counts?
options: They have negative correlation by definition

questions.question: A model has arrival counts whose distribution changes with calendar time, not just interval length. Which Poisson-process assumption is suspect?
options: The fact that counts are random.
The existence of an index set

questions.question: Why are exponential interarrival times natural for a Poisson process?
options: Poisson counts are always continuous waiting times
Every stochastic process has exponential interarrival times.
The constant-rate independent increments give memoryless waiting

questions.question: What does $N_t$ represent in a Poisson process?
options: $N_t$ is a count by time $t$, not the waiting time between arrivals.
$N_t$ is the length of the next interarrival time after $t$.
$N_t$ is the probability that no arrival has ever occurred.
$N_t$ is the fixed rate parameter of the process.

questions.question: If $\lambda=2$ and an interval has length $0$, what is the parameter of the increment count?
A proposed Poisson process has $\lambda=-4$. What is wrong?
options: The rate parameter must be positive
The process must be indexed by cards
